result.summary: I read the Tactics code and the FC 27 data captured today, and did a light read-only static check of the game image. The result changes the plan. The gameplay sliders already have a working write path: the game reads per-side game variables named GAMEPLAY_CUSTOMIZATION/<SLIDER>_USER and _CPU. There are 29 names per side: sprint speed, acceleration, pass error and speed, shot error and speed, trap and intercept-trap error, ball deflection error, dribble error, GK ability, defensive line height, line length, line width, marking, run frequency, full-back positioning, buildup speed, shot, cross and dribble frequency, tackling and fouls. One settings function in FC27.exe 1.0.140.64835 (around 0x1442DC794) loops over them and calls the same GetInt (0x140856DB4) that Turbo's injury overrides go through. For each slider it does byte[settings+0x331+2*(side*0x27+id)] = GetInt(name, current byte). gamevars_fc27.txt missed these names because its scan only finds a string loaded right before the call. So the existing, played-match-proven gv::apply/SetInt channel can drive all 11 "no write path" sliders. Because the _CPU names exist, it can also give per-fixture, CPU-only opposition variety in line height, width, compactness, marking, runs, tempo, crossing, shooting, dribbling and aggression. Whether each value changes play, and whether it holds under Authentic, still needs one played-match A/B test per slider. The other channels came out like this. The Attribulator route is unavailable: Live Editor 27.1.2 lacks the GameplayAttribulatorSetVar and GameplayAttribulatorGetVarType natives in a real-game probe. The Tactics tab's writes to cm_mentalities are invisible in matches and overwritten at the next save: the runtime TeamSheetService loads cm_teamsheets/cm_mentalities once at career load and writes them back at every save. Which table the CPU's tactic is read from is unknown. The runtime TeamSheet SetSheet game call is the only route for formation, roles/focus, build-up and defensive approach that is likely to work, but its layout past +0xC4 is unmapped and Turbo's signature table has no TeamSheet entries yet. In the code, the main changes are: an effect-verification flag on each slider separate from SliderStatus; GameVar bindings with several targets or per side; a pure core per-fixture engine driven from App instead of from the tab's static state; and fixing the opposition seed, which today uses the Lua session's load counter and today's date, so the same fixture gets a new profile after a reload or a day advance. Tests and sizes for each item are listed below.

findings.topic: Slider registry: statuses, bindings and validation
findings.claim: Each slider has one SliderStatus out of Live, DB, Local, Preview and RE, plus a SliderEvidence and a BindingKind out of None, GameVar, DbField and Turbo. writes_game() is true only for Live and DB. validate_registry enforces Live = GameVar + Real, DB = DbField, RE = no binding. Nothing records whether the effect was seen in a played match. So OVERRIDE_MATCH_DIFFICULTY (accepted, no visible effect) shows the same green [Live] badge as the injury sliders that were verified in a match today.

findings.topic: The 11 gameplay sliders are per-side game variables
findings.claim: FC27.exe contains GAMEPLAY_CUSTOMIZATION/<X>_USER and _CPU names for SPRINT_SPEED, ACCELERATION, SHOT_ERROR, SHOT_SPEED, PASS_ERROR, PASS_SPEED, PASS_ANGLE_ERROR, HEADER_SHOT/PASS_ACCURACY, TRAP_ERROR, INTERCEPT_TRAP_ERROR, BALL_DEFLECTION_ERROR, DRIBBLE_ERROR, TACKLE_ACCURACY, GK_ABILITY, POS_DEF_LINE_HEIGHT, POS_LINE_LENGTH, POS_LINE_WIDTH, POS_MARKING, POS_RUN_FREQUENCY, POS_FULL_BACK, DEFENDING_AGGRESSION, STAND/SLIDE_TACKLE_FREQUENCY, PROFESSIONAL_FOUL_FREQUENCY, NORMAL_SHOT_FREQUENCY, BUILDUP_SPEED, SKILL_MOVE_FREQUENCY, NORMAL/EARLY_CROSSING_FREQUENCY, FIRST_TOUCH_PASS_FREQUENCY, DRIBBLE_FREQUENCY and INJURY_*. Function ~0x1442DC794 builds {id, name} arrays of them in six groups (CPU and USER x basic, positioning, frequency) and hands each to 0x1442D8260. That function does byte[settings+0x331+2*(side*0x27+id)] = GetInt(name, current byte), with GetInt = 0x140856DB4, the same reader gv::apply targets. A name that is not set returns the current value, so the menu or preset value stays. The loop has no gameplay-type condition around it.

findings.topic: Game-variable pipeline (Apply, clear, kill switches)
findings.claim: Apply: ui_tactics apply_changes -> effective_writes -> app.match_setup->set_var. Host queue_var runs gv::apply on the game thread (SetInt plus read-back). A Live slider switched off is cleared with clear_var. The banner's Clear calls clear_all, and App::~App calls tactics_clear_on_exit. Kill switches: tactics_off.txt (polled every 2 s and re-checked at every write), call_gamevar_off.txt (host, per job) and game_hooks_allowed. Overrides survive career loads in a session but not a game restart. Arena room is about 95 KB and the node pool holds 8192 (1408 used), enough for about 60 more names at about 80 bytes each. gv::apply refuses non-int variables (type != 2); SetFloat 0x14154F324 has no Turbo path.

findings.topic: DB channel: cm_mentalities is overwritten by the runtime sheet
findings.claim: cm_teamsheets and cm_mentalities are read into GameServices::CachedTeamSheetService only at LoadGameComplete (LoadTeamSheets). FCECommsManager::TriggerSave writes every runtime sheet back with WriteTeamSheet (UPSERT cm_teamsheets + cm_mentalities). So the Tactics tab's writes to cm_mentalities (team.line_depth, team.buildup_play) are invisible in matches and replaced at the next save. In the real save cm_mentalities has 1 row (the user's tactic).

findings.topic: What FC 27 actually stores for a tactic
findings.claim: The user's tactic row (cm_mentalities) holds only buildupplay 0..3, defensivedepth 1..128, presetid, sourceformationid, position0..10, offsets, playerid0..10 and pos0..10role (0..65535), plus tactic_name and activetactic. It has no defensivestyle, chancecreation, widths or players-in-box, which exist only in `mentalities` (4001 rows, likely about 5 presets per club). That matches the game's Edit Tactic screen: a preset, a formation, Build-Up Style, Defensive Approach, and a role and focus per slot. How posNrole encodes role and focus is unknown; cm_role_synergies (roleid, specid, positionid) suggests the role and focus ids are each 0..255. teamformationteamstylelinks has 0 rows in the real save.

findings.claim: FixtureId.career = load_gen, a Lua-session counter that goes up on every career load, and matchday = today's date. The same fixture therefore gets a different profile after a reload, a game restart or a day advance. That contradicts plan section 4 ("same fixture gets the same profile in a given career").

findings.claim: Profiles store slider keys, values and enabled flags; unknown keys are kept verbatim. findings.topic: Squad roles are not tactic roles
findings.claim: squad_role.lua, team_mass.lua and ui_role_rules.cpp handle squad STATUS (Crucial..Prospect) in the PlayerStatusManager vector, with a SEASON_RESET re-apply and role_reapply_off.txt. They do not touch per-slot tactic role and focus. Likewise players.role1..9 (pos.role1..9, DB/Real) are a player's own role list, not the role of a team-sheet slot. Their structure (GUI rule editor, then app.send op run, a result routed by label prefix in App::tick, a kill switch file polled every 2 s) is the template for any channel that needs Lua.

channels.name: A. Game variables (GAMEPLAY_CUSTOMIZATION/*_USER|_CPU and others) through the existing gv::apply/SetInt

Add per_side rows match.<x>_user/_cpu and a 'Team positioning' and 'Frequencies' group; add opp.* CPU rows (absolute values or offsets). [M] (3) sliders.h: new field `SliderEffect effect {Verified, Untested, NoEffectSeen}` plus `effect_note` ("2026-10-07 injuries 1'/3'/5'"), shown separately from SliderStatus; `base_key` (string) for offset sliders, replacing the hard-coded base_slider_of (ui_tactics.cpp:203-217); validate_registry: Verified needs a note, offsets need a base_key [S]. OppProfile gets cpu_vars (name -> clamp 0..100 of base+delta); opp_rules.cpp valid_target uses writes_game() [M]. (6) New pure core/match_apply.{h,cpp}: plan_fixture(next fixture from fce::next_fixture, user team, save uid, active match profile, opposition params, rules) -> {key, writes}; diff(applied, planned) -> sets and clears; never emits a _USER name from the opposition [M]. (7) App: a member OppAuto (ledger name -> value plus fixture key) driven from App::tick when the in-game date or next fixture changes (no per-frame memory reads); sends match_setup->set_var/clear_var; also clears when no fixture is found. tactics_clear_on_exit counts these writes. Kill switches: tactics_off.txt, call_gamevar_off.txt, new opp_auto_off.txt [M]. (8) Seed fix: FixtureId.career from GetSaveUID published in bridge_state (bridge.lua collect_state plus BridgeState.save_uid), matchday = fixture date or fixture id, home/away from the fixture [S]. Re-apply: values die with the process and survive career loads, so wire TacticProfileStore::set_active to an 'apply automatically' checkbox and re-send the active Match profile once per Lua session (the ui_reapply.cpp maybe_reapply pattern, keyed by session not load_gen); the per-fixture engine recomputes on connect. Clear: clear_var per name; Clear overrides; on exit. Tests: native test_tactics_core: every Live target is gv::known with the slider range inside the known range; every GAMEPLAY_CUSTOMIZATION name passes gv::check_name and the arena total is under 8 KB; Verified sliders carry a note; kCpuVars only produces *_CPU names; cpu_vars are deterministic for a FixtureId, clamped 0..100 and within max_delta of the base; mode 'none' gives no writes. test_main/FakeMatchSetup: match_apply sends nothing when the key is unchanged, clear_var for a dropped name, clear-all when there is no fixture, nothing when opp_auto_off.txt or tactics_off.txt exists. test_tactics_tab UI: the Opposition scope's 'apply automatically per fixture' sends only *_CPU names, the banner lists them, Clear overrides clears them. Lua t07_bridge: bridge_state carries save_uid.
channels.risk: These are EA's own gameplay-customization values, overridden in memory: the menu stays on Authentic and untouched, the same way the injury override works, but the user should approve this reading of 'never touch EA's slider menu'. They apply to every played match in the process (not saved, also reach online), so the banner and clear-on-exit matter. If the loop only runs at boot or game-mode setup rather than per match, values set in the hub may only apply after the next match setup; the A/B test settles it. Without reading the settings block, Turbo does not know the Authentic base value, so offsets are relative to 50.
channels.verification_test: One slider at a time, from the same autosave (turbo04), extreme values, CPU side only, Authentic and Dynamic Opposition kept on: (1) SPRINT_SPEED_CPU=0 and ACCELERATION_CPU=0. Pass: the CPU's players are clearly slower in foot races in the first 5 minutes. Then clear, reload and replay as the control. (2) GK_ABILITY_CPU=0 plus your long shots: easy goals compared with the control. (3) PASS_ERROR_CPU=100: CPU pass accuracy in Match Facts at least 15 points lower than the control. (4) POS_DEF_LINE_HEIGHT_CPU=100 against 0: the CPU's back line sits at halfway against the edge of the box during your build-up (radar, pause screenshots at the same minute). Also set one of them after the pre-match screen to learn when it is read. Record turbo_gui.log 'gamevar set ... ok' lines and screenshots. A slider counts as Verified only when both repeats show a clear difference.

result.summary: FC 27 career mode keeps a team's tactic in two places, one for your club and one for CPU clubs, and Turbo's Tactics tab currently writes to neither in a way that can take effect. YOUR club's tactics live in cm_mentalities (up to 5 tactics per team sheet, key teamid+teamsheetid+mentalityid, active = activetactic 1) and cm_teamsheets. Those rows are only read once, at career load, into the game's runtime team-sheet service, and the runtime copy is written back over them at every save (code: LoadTeamSheets 0x147B5DB4C -> reader 0x147B9B9A4; WriteTeamSheet -> writer 0x147B96DD8). So a Turbo DB edit of your own tactic is never seen in game and is lost at the next save. CPU clubs have NO cm_mentalities rows (rows=1, Napoli only). Their live tactic is default_mentalities (870 rows, one per team). The game copies it to cm_default_mentalities at every save (0x147B60308 called from TriggerSave) and restores it from there at load (0x147B5FF78 called from LoadGameComplete). The match-side code reads it with "SELECT * FROM default_mentalities WHERE teamid = %d", including pos0role..pos10role, buildupplay and defensivedepth. The FC 27 tactic itself is small: formation (sourceformationid, formationfullnameid, formationaudioid, position0..10, offsets), buildupplay 0..3 (Build-Up Style), defensivedepth 1..100 (Defensive Approach), pos{n}role per slot (Role + focus, encoding unknown) and presetid / tactic_name / code. Width, players in box, chance creation and offensive/defensive style exist only in the legacy `mentalities` table (4001 rows, the non-career team-sheet service), and that is where Turbo writes them today. players.role1..9 are the player's Role+/Role++ familiarity, not the role of a slot. CPU style can also be driven by team AI traits (teams.trait1vweak/vequal/vstrong, a 23-bit mask labelled Tiki Taka, Possession, Counter Attack, Direct, Harass, Italian Defense and so on; teams.opponentweak/strongthreshold; manager.trait1v*), which feed the match team data. Proposed write sets: CPU style, roles and formation go into default_mentalities (plus traits in teams and manager), then the career is saved and reloaded before a played match. For your own club the only real routes are the runtime TeamSheet (an L3 game call) or the game's own Edit Tactic screen. Every write set comes with an in-game A/B test below. Nothing here has been tested in a match yet.

result.summary: I found no in-game proof yet. Static code, mostly from the dumped image of the previous build (6AB9813C, fc27_image.bin), plus repo docs, shows two separate tactic paths: one for the user's club and one for CPU clubs. User club: the tactic lives in a runtime object, GameServices::CachedTeamSheetService (service 0x113EA820). The game reads cm_teamsheets and cm_mentalities into it once, when the career loads, and writes it back over both tables at every save. Turbo's current Tactics-tab writes to cm_mentalities therefore never reach a match and are reverted at the next save. I decoded where the tactic sits inside the runtime team sheet: build-up style, line depth, formation, and each slot's position, offsets and role (role and focus), all at known offsets. A match-setup function copies the formation and each slot's role from this object into the match. So for the user's club Turbo must edit this runtime object on the game thread through the game's own SetSheet call. The legacy columns (widths, chance creation, players in box, attacking/defensive style) only exist in the old `mentalities` table and cannot affect the user's club. CPU clubs have no cm_* rows. Their sheets most likely come from the database-backed sheet service, which reads `teamsheets`, `mentalities`, `default_*` and `formations`. A match team builder also reads `teams` live for each side: buildupplay, defensivedepth, opponent strong/weak thresholds and the trait1vweak/equal/strong fields. Those trait fields are the game's own CPU style system: a 23-bit mask (Tiki-Taka, Possession, Counter Attack, Direct, Crossing, Harass, Italian Defense, No Pressure and others) chosen by opponent strength. That is the natural channel for opposition variety. I also found about 90 GAMEPLAY_CUSTOMIZATION/*_USER and _CPU game variables (team positioning, build-up speed, sprint, pass and shot error and more). The game reads them with the same GetInt override already proven for injuries, but docs/re/gamevars_fc27.txt misses them. That gives a per-side team-shape channel with no new hook. When the game reads them, and whether they work under Authentic, is unknown. All addresses are from the old build and must be re-checked on build 6AC07E31-2145C000; the team-sheet functions are in scripts/re/realtime_signatures.json but not in Turbo's built-in signature table. My read-only analysis helpers are in C:\Users\cmode\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--FC-27-Live-Editor\8726d1ac-4c08-4abf-a892-1a930213a680\scratchpad\re\ (sgrep.py, xr.py, dz.py, fnstr.py, qw.py, ptab.py, srange.py). They use the repo's scripts/re/rx_jobs.py and wrote nothing to the repo.

findings.topic: User club: the runtime team sheet is the master copy
findings.claim: The user's team sheet and its tactics live in GameServices::CachedTeamSheetService (service id 0x113EA820). cm_teamsheets and cm_mentalities are read into it only at career load: LoadGameComplete 0x147CA102C calls LoadTeamSheets 0x147B5DB4C, which uses the field reader 0x147B9B9A4. Every save writes them back: TriggerSave 0x147B99DE4 calls WriteTeamSheet 0x147B9616C, which uses the cm_mentalities writer 0x147B96DD8. No other code copies cm_mentalities values into the runtime.
findings.evidence: docs/re/realtime_transfers.md:170-187; scripts/re/realtime_signatures.json:94-117. Image xrefs of the string "cm_mentalities" (0x14AFF3580): only 0x147B5DB4C (load), 0x147B5F998 (delete all), 0x147B718D4, 0x147B94AC0 (delete row) and 0x147B960A8 (write). The reader 0x147B9B9A4 has one caller, 0x147B5DE2F, inside LoadTeamSheets.

findings.topic: Turbo 2.0 Tactics tab: the user club's DB writes cannot work
findings.claim: Writes to cm_mentalities.defensivedepth and cm_mentalities.buildupplay for the user's club are not read during the session. The runtime sheet overwrites them at the next save, so they can never persist. A reload cannot pick them up either, because the in-memory edit is overwritten before the save is written. The user club's rows in `mentalities` are not its active career tactic.
findings.evidence: turbogui/src/core/sliders.cpp:199-233 lists the targets (teams.defensivedepth, cm_mentalities.defensivedepth/buildupplay, mentalities.*). turbogui/src/ui/ui_tactics.cpp:304-322 and turbogui/src/core/tactics_db.cpp:252-273 pick the row (activetactic, else first). Follows from the finding above.

findings.topic: Runtime tactic record layout (decoded from the cm_mentalities writer)
findings.claim: TeamSheet (0x288 bytes): +0 teamsheetid, +4 teamid, +0xC4 52 int32 player ids, +0x1B0 pointer to an array of tactic records of 0xF8 bytes each. A record's index is mentalityid % 5 and the count comes from 0x1410BE030(sheet). Tactic record: +0x00 tactic_name (EASTL string, short-string flag at +0xF), +0x68 code (string), +0x80 activetactic (u8), +0x84 presetid, +0xA4 defensivedepth, +0xB0 buildupplay, +0xC0 formationfullnameid, +0xC4 sourceformationid (written last), +0xC8 formationaudioid, +0xD0 sourceformationid (written first). +0xD8/+0xE0 is an eastl::vector of 0x48-byte slot entries: +0 playerid, +4 position, +8 offset x (float), +0xC offset y (float), +0x30 pos{n}role. Each slot also has +0x10/+0x14, which are never written to the DB.
findings.evidence: Disassembly of 0x147B96DD8. Field-name pointer tables: 0x14A118050 offset{n}y, 0x14A1180B0 offset{n}x, 0x14A118110 position{n}, 0x14A118170 pos{n}role. WriteTeamSheet passes the TeamSheet as r8 at 0x147B965DA. Compare scripts/re/realtime_signatures.json:897.

findings.topic: How the sheet's tactic reaches a match
findings.claim: 0x148037DC8 resolves TeamSheetService 0x113EA820 and converts a tactic's formation part (record+0xC0) into the match team setup. For up to 11 slots it copies position (+4), offsets (+8/+0xC), +0x10, +0x14 and the slot role (+0x30) into the output, with the roles at out+0x118+4*i. 0x148037D10 reads buildupplay and defensivedepth and converts them. Callers are the formation-list builders 0x148041070 and 0x148041460 (formations, customformations, ssfformations). Slot role and formation are therefore real match inputs.

findings.topic: SetSheet and the team-sheet signatures
findings.claim: SetSheet(svc, modeId, sheet) is vtable slot 24 at 0x145E45C40. It calls vf[0x5B0]; if the sheet's teamsheetid equals vf[0xB8](teamid), the team's current sheet, it also calls vf[0xF8](sheet). RemovePlayerFromTeamSheets 0x145E3ED90 fetches the sheet via vf[0x588], vf[0x590] or vf[0x598] before SetSheet, which is the game's own get-modify-set pattern. None of the team-sheet functions is in Turbo's built-in signature table; they are only in scripts/re/realtime_signatures.json, for the old build.
findings.evidence: Disassembly 0x145E45C40-0x145E45C9F and 0x145E3ED90. scripts/re/realtime_signatures.json:430-461, 606-613. Grepping turbogui/src/core/sigscan.cpp for "sheet" finds nothing.

findings.topic: Safety infrastructure already in place
findings.claim: run_on_game_thread runs queued jobs after the MainLoop frame body (at most 32 per frame) or on the Lua pump; gv::apply uses the game's own SetInt under its writer lock, with read-back and the call_gamevar_off.txt kill switch. The dev service runs on its own background thread (dev_thread), so its `write` op is not game-thread safe; reads use ProcessMemory and fail without crashing. Lesson from the standings crash: never call an object found by vtable search.

channels.how: Add a new native game call (next mailbox op, modelled on player_move). Run it with run_on_game_thread, only in the career hub, not while Team Management is open, the SimDayManager is busy, a match is running or a save is in progress. Re-resolve every address by signature on 6AC07E31: SetSheet, the cached-service vtable and the service registry Find. Get the service through the registry's Find(0x113EA820), as MovePlayerLink does, and check its vtable. Fetch the user's sheet with the service's own getter (one of slots 0x588/0x590/0x598 used by RemovePlayerFromTeamSheets; identify which). Check teamid equals the user club, the tactic count is 1..5, the active record has activetactic 1, the slot vector holds 11 entries of 0x48 bytes, and every value is inside the GetDBMeta range. Copy the sheet, change only the requested fields, call SetSheet (slot 24), then read back. Turbo never saves; the game's next save writes the change to cm_mentalities. Kill switches: tactics_off.txt plus a new call_team_sheet_off.txt.

RE procedure for the user, read-only dev service, throwaway career turbo04, game in the career hub with Team Management closed. (1) Find the runtime sheet: {"op":"find","pattern":"5C 6F 03 00 0E 35 03 00 27 BA 03 00","writable":true,"max":50}. These are the little-endian sheet slots 0-2: 225116, 217870, 244263. For each hit H, read H-0xC4 for 0x288 bytes and require +4 == 0x30 (team 48). (2) ptrs at sheet+0x1B0 gives T. Read T for 0xF8 bytes: expect the tactic name in ASCII at T+0, activetactic 1 at +0x80, depth 30 or less at +0xA4, a value 0..3 at +0xB0, and a vector at +0xD8/+0xE0 whose size is 0x318. Read the vector (11 slots x 0x48). (3) In Edit Tactic, step Build-Up Style through every option; after each, go back to the hub and re-read T+0xA0..0xB8 to build the label table. (4) Same for Defensive Approach, reading +0xA4. (5) Change one player's role, then his focus, across 6-8 combinations, and re-read slot +0x30 (also +0x10/+0x14) to derive the encoding. (6) Change the formation, for example 4-4-1-1 MIDFIELD to 4-3-3, and re-read +0xC0..+0xD4 plus every slot's position and offsets. (7) Save in game and extend probe_tactics to dump the cm_mentalities row: its values must equal the runtime ones, which proves both the layout and the write-back. (8) CPU: dump Forest's `teamsheets`/`default_teamsheets` player ids, `mentalities` rows and `teams` style and trait fields with a Lua probe. Search memory for its first three line-up ids: a hit means CPU sheets are cached; no hit means they are built from the DB. Never use the dev service `write`, because it runs off the game thread.

result.summary: FC 27 gives a manager only a few tactical controls for each team. These are a formation, a Build-Up Style (Short Passing, Balanced or Counter) and a Defensive Approach (Deep, Balanced, High or Aggressive). The Defensive Approach is tied to a Line Height of 1-100, in bands 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and 91-100. Each of the 11 slots also gets a Role and a Focus, a team can save up to 5 tactics, and in career mode the tactic also carries a "Tactical Vision" preset (Standard, Possession, High Pressing and so on). Set-piece takers and corner assignments are separate. During a match the manager has Tactical Focus (Default, Attacking or Defending, which moves the tactic one step) and Quick Tactics (Offside Trap, Team Press, Overload Set Pieces, Get In Box). FC 25 removed several old controls: attacking and defensive width, chance creation, pressure, players in box, players at corners and free kicks, work rates and player instructions. EA's FC 25 FC IQ notes say so, and the career tactic table cm_mentalities has none of those fields. Turbo's Tactics tab still binds 7 sliders and a 7-step "mentality" to legacy `mentalities` fields or to controls FC 27 does not have. Section 8 of the 2.0 plan describes the FIFA 22-FC 24 tactic model and is out of date. The game's sliders are set per side, not per team: User/CPU in Game Type Settings, and CPU Opponent/CPU Teammate in CPU Sliders. Third-party guides give a 1-99 range with a default of 50. EA confirms 25 new gameplay sliders and 10 new CPU sliders in FC 27. Under Authentic the Game Type rows are greyed out (your screenshot), and Authentic reads a separate Attribulator database called "simulation". For opponent tactics, the AI Behaviour setting offers Tactical, Dynamic or Custom. Only third-party guides describe Dynamic as adapting during a match, and I found no game text called "Dynamic Opposition". EA says CPU teams have distinct styles and that AI managers impose their Tactical Vision on a club. Live Editor's Formation Editor wiki says the CPU never changes formation. That means the only per-team way to vary opponents is to edit their tactic rows in the database before kick-off, and nobody has tested that in a match yet. Of the Football Manager (FM) instructions, only formation, role and duty, defensive line, attacking transition, set-piece takers and roughly line of engagement map onto FC 27. Width, marking, compactness, runs, tackling, tempo, crossing and dribbling can only be approximated with sliders that apply to a whole side, and most of those exist only for the CPU. FC 27 has nothing equivalent to separate in-possession and out-of-possession shapes, opposition or player instructions, time-wasting, goalkeeper distribution, pressing traps or flank focus. Turbo has four channels that respect the user's preferences: DB tactic rows, teamsheets, game variables, and the Attribulator on the simulation database.

findings.topic: How the AI chooses opponent tactics (Tactical vs Dynamic)
findings.claim: Tactical keeps a CPU team close to its preferred style, even after a red card or losing its playmaker. Dynamic uses that style only as a base and adapts during the match, for example forcing play wide when that area produces chances, or pushing a False 9 up as a target man. Custom exposes the sliders. Only third-party guides describe this; I found no EA text. A FC 27 forum user reports switching from Dynamic to custom CPU behaviour, which confirms the option exists. No source anywhere uses the label 'Dynamic Opposition', which is most likely the user's name for AI Behaviour: Dynamic.

result.summary: I found a full slider override family in FC27.exe that docs/re/gamevars_fc27.txt misses. That file was built only from direct GetInt (0x140856DB4) call sites. Re-running scripts/re/gv_names.py on the GetFloat, int-or-zero and Exists readers finds 1191 more names. The family is 65 GAMEPLAY_CUSTOMIZATION/*_USER and *_CPU names: 16 error/speed sliders (sprint, acceleration, shot/pass error and speed, trap error, GK ability is in the positioning group, and so on), 7 positioning sliders (marking, line length, line width, defensive line height, run frequency, full back, GK ability), the 11 new 'CPU sliders' (defending aggression, slide/stand tackle frequency, shot frequency, build-up speed, ...) and POWER_BAR_SPEED_USER. They are read in one function, 0x1442DC794, which uses GetInt(name, current byte) and writes them into a 0x1268-byte GameSettings slider block: 50 sets x 39 sliders x {user, cpu} bytes, scale 0..100 with 50 neutral, and in match byte x 0.01. That function is the GameSettings reset (it also sets half length 6 and weather 0). In the mode match setup, the block is then rebuilt from the profile settings, by setting id, for all 50 sets (0x14807E7E4 via 0x1480293A4). So these overrides are most likely lost before kick-off (ASSESSED). Only the separate Exists-gated injury reads (_CPUAI names, 0x140FEBDB4) were proven today. The code also shows how Authentic works. When the match copies the block (0x141EBCEA4), 8 sliders whose byte is exactly 50 get gameplay-type preset values (sprint, acceleration, trap error, pass speed, slider 33, line length, line width, run frequency), and any non-50 byte is kept (VERIFIED in code at 0x141EBD184). So a Turbo value that reaches the block before or at the match copy should work with Authentic still selected. The realistic channels are: (a) the gamevars, cheap to test with one decisive injury test; (b) a pre-match byte write into the block, or a game call to the game's own copy-and-recompute pair 0x141EBCEA4 / 0x141EBD1C4 in the match; (c) per-team AI difficulty floats OVERRIDE_{HOME,AWAY}_{OFFENSE,DEFENSE}_DIFFICULTY, which are read after the session's difficulty, so they probably survive. The Attribulator route does not exist in Live Editor 27.1.2: GameplayAttribulator* and Aardvark* natives are absent. Writing the profile setting ids would amount to editing EA's slider menu, which the user ruled out. All addresses are from the 1.0.140.64835 image and must be re-signatured for build 6AC07E31-2145C000.

findings.topic: Slider block layout and value scale
findings.claim: The GameSettings slider block is 0x1268 bytes. Offset 0x000: 50 sets x 39 sliders x {USER byte, CPU byte} (stride 0x4E). Offset 0x1110: positioning, 2 sets x 7 x {U,C}. Offset 0x112C: power bar, 22 slots x 2. Offset 0x1158: CPU-AI user array. Offset 0x1178: CPU-AI CPU array. Defaults come from a config with fallback 50. Range 0..100 with 50 neutral. In the match the getter returns byte x 0.01 (and 0.5 if the set index is 50 or more). Values above 100 are not range-checked and would go past 1.0. Only slider indices 0-15 have game variables; the other 23 of the 39 per side are the new FC 27 sliders (chip, finesse, power and low-driven shot error/speed; lob, cross, through and lobbed-through pass error/speed; dribble touch intervals; jockey speeds; physicality impact; GK and outfield ball-deflection control) and have no game variable.
findings.evidence: 0x14185B9DC: init loops of 50 x 0x27 x 2, then 2 x 7 at +0x1110 (index (s+0x138)*7), 22 at +0x112C, 0x32 fill at +0x1158; default getter 0x1442C5904 (+0x30 user / +0x38 cpu, fallback r8 = 50). Getter 0x141331480: movzx [set*0x27+i)*2 + 0x5D20 + isCpu] then vmulss by 0.01 (0x14962A018); r10d >= 0x32 returns 0.5. FC 27 slider enum strings at 0x14A8C0528 to 0x14A8C0F28.

findings.topic: User vs CPU split
findings.claim: Byte +0 is the USER value and +1 the CPU value. In the match the getter adds 1 when the side's control flag [ctrl + teamIndex + 0x35A1] is set, so the human-controlled team uses USER values and the AI team uses CPU values. For the CPU-AI group the _USER names most likely mean 'CPU teammates' and _CPU 'CPU opponent', matching the FC 27 split into 'CPU Teammate' and 'CPU Opponent'.
findings.evidence: 0x141331480 to 0x1413314E3 (r8 = flag != 0; lea rax,[r11+r8]). Name-to-offset mapping in 0x1442D8260 (+0x331, _CPU) and 0x1442D82F4 (+0x330, _USER). Second sentence assessed from docs/TURBO_2_0_PLAN.md:353.

findings.topic: Match copy and Authentic substitution
findings.claim: At match setup the game copies the block from GameSettings (Y+0x10120) to the match object (M+0x5D20). It then touches 8 sliders in all 50 sets, user and CPU: sprint (index 0), acceleration (1), trap error (6), pass speed (13), slider 33, and positioning line length, line width and run frequency. Each of these bytes is replaced only if it equals 50. The replacement comes from a gameplay-type config: mode 0 uses one float, mode 2 another, any other mode keeps 50. A non-50 byte is kept. So a Turbo value other than 50 survives Authentic, and a value of exactly 50 means 'the game decides'.
findings.evidence: 0x141EBCEA4: memcpy(this+0x5D20, src, 0x1268), then jmp 0x141EBCECC (loop of 50 sets and 2 positioning sets, offsets 0x5D20/21, 0x5D22/23, 0x5D2C/2D, 0x5D3A/3B, 0x5D62/63, 0x6E32/33, 0x6E34/35, 0x6E38/39). 0x141EBD184: edx==0 uses xmm2, edx==2 uses xmm3, otherwise 50.0; the byte is written only if it was 0x32 (cmp al,0x32). Callers 0x141881AB4 (copy from [G+0xA60]+0x10120 to [G+0xFC8]), 0x146A22C80, 0x14164EBF4, 0x141EBCCC4, 0x14291EF54, 0x146A498D9.

findings.topic: Which mode is Authentic
findings.claim: The substitution mode is read from Y+0xFFA4, which is GameSettings+0x1B4. The reset fills that field from GAME_SPEED (default 1). The mode setup then overwrites it from the session (+0x1EE0). Which number means Authentic, Competitive or Custom is unknown. A mode with no substitution (1) fits Custom.
findings.evidence: 0x141EBCEDB: edi = [[[M+0x5D18]+0xA60]+0xFFA4]. 0x1442DC7F9: GAME_SPEED stored to [rsi+0x1B4]. 0x14802AB9B: [r14+0x1B4] = [src+0x1EE0]. 0x1447BB8BC: [rsi+0x1B4] = [r14+0x10]. GameSettings = Y+0xFDF0 because three offsets agree: +0x330 = 0x10120, +0x107 = 0xFEF7 (block-init flag in 0x146A22CCC and 0x1442DCA24), +0x1B4 = 0xFFA4.

findings.topic: Do the GAMEPLAY_CUSTOMIZATION slider game variables reach a match?
findings.claim: Probably not. 0x1442DC794 is a defaults reset (it sets half length 6, weather 0, game speed 1). The mode match setup calls it first, through Arxan stub 0x1442DD200, then applies the real settings. A later builder (0x14802BAD0 to 0x1480293A4 to 0x14807E7E4) rewrites the whole block for all 50 sets from profile setting ids (CPU 0xB0-0xD4, USER 0xDC-0x100, slider 10 forced to 50). The front-end path (0x1447BB230) either copies settings or fills sets with 50. Either way the reset-time overrides are overwritten. The only proven slider-style override is the separate Exists-gated injury read (_CPUAI and INJURY_*_USER, 0x140FEBDB4), which falls back to the block byte when the variable is absent.

findings.topic: In-match recompute
findings.claim: After the copy, 0x141EBD1C4 converts slider bytes into float tables for 2 teams x 25 sets, scaled by a per-team difficulty multiplier and interpolated between per-slider minimum and maximum values. Writing M+0x5D20 in the middle of a match would therefore reach direct getter readers but not these precomputed tables. The game's own in-match update (0x146A22C80, probably the pause-menu slider change) runs memcpy into Y+0x10120, then 0x141EBCEA4, block init and 0x141EBD1C4 again.

findings.topic: Per-team AI difficulty game variables
findings.claim: OVERRIDE_{HOME,AWAY}_{OFFENSE,DEFENSE}_DIFFICULTY are float values from 0 to 1. Levels 0-5 map to 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0. The mode match setup reads them after the session's per-team levels, with the current value as default, so they probably survive into the match. GetFloat accepts integer variables, so Turbo's SetInt can express only 0 (Beginner) or 1 (Legendary); in-between values need the game's SetFloat (0x14154F324, type 3). The variables are keyed by home/away, not user/CPU.

findings.topic: GAME_SPEED
findings.claim: GAME_SPEED feeds the gameplay-type mode field (GameSettings+0x1B4), not a speed scale. Setting it could switch the gameplay type away from Authentic, and the mode setup overwrites it anyway. Turbo must never set it. CPUAI_PLAYER_BASED_DIFFICULTY_{HOME,AWAY} and ADAPTIVE_DIFFICULTY/* may relate to Dynamic Opposition (unknown) and should also stay untouched.

findings.topic: OVERRIDE_ERROR_ATTRIBUTE
findings.claim: A float game variable read on every action in the error code. Its default is the player's own value and the result is clamped to [0, 2.4]. It is global, both teams, with no user/CPU split, and is probably read live during the match. Whether it governs pass, shot or touch error is unknown.

findings.topic: Turbo code today
findings.claim: Turbo's game-variable writer only handles integers and refuses an existing non-integer variable. The UI offers only 9 known variables. The 11 gameplay sliders are status RE with no binding. Adding any of the names above requires new KnownVar or SliderDef entries; the store mechanism itself accepts any name of A-Z, 0-9, _ and /. The dev service already has read, find (with ?? wildcards) and write operations for read-only probes and test writes.
